title: رئيس الاتحاد الإسباني يتحدى المغاربة بتصريح حاسم: لا تفاوض

title: ضربة مزدوجة.. تأكد غياب ثنائي الجزائر عن مواجهة توجو

body: Weird Weekend Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Rick and Ted have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager . What's the fastest you've ever fallen in love with a game? I think I have a new record: about 0.3 seconds into CultGame , when launching it from Steam spawned not a regular game window, but a command prompt instance. Perfection. Chef's kiss. No notes. Like the Bay 12 games (Dwarf Fortress and especially Liberal Crime Squad ) it clearly takes inspiration from, CultGame is gloriously text-based. Its art is ASCII, its options selected by tippy-tapping the numpad, its maps are carpets of symbols: lurid at signs and hashes as far as the eye can see. It's a management game, first and foremost. Once you have generated a world and a history for it, you choose the precise nature of cult leader you wish to be: Defector Cleric, Occult Scholar, Con Artist, or Lunatic, and off you go. title: Formula 1 just found a bizarre financial supporter in horse girl gacha Umamusume: Pretty Derby
summary: I'm here for it, though.
body: What is Formula 1 if not just very fast, mechanical horse racing? Surely I'm not the only one who has asked that question, especially considering the Japanese Grand Prix leg of the 2027 F1 World Championship has just revealed that Cygame's horse girl gacha Umamusume: Pretty Derby has become a founding partner. What does that mean in practice? Well, according to a press release, founding partners are "the highest tier supporters of the F1 Japanese Grand Prix," where they "bring additional value to the event while helping to shape the direction of its growth. Through marketing, promotional activities, and creating new experiences for fans, Umamusume will continue contributing to the long term growth of the Japanese Grand Prix." (Image credit: Cygames, Inc.) In layman's terms, that'll be a tidy sum of money invested into the Japanese Grand Prix, and in Umamusume's case it also means slapping its name on one of Suzuka Circuit's iconic corners—changing the name from the 130R corner to Umamusume 130R for around a year.
